scope: Proposition 7.4 (Regularity of the measure moments) of the manuscript “A Charged Reduction of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality in Spatial Dimensions at Least Four” (preprints/A-Charged-Reduction-of-the-Spacetime-Penrose-Inequality-in-Spatial-Dimensions-at-Least-Four-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3e5e445d305051a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 58. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the open exterior the moments are functions satisfying the first Killing initial data (KID) equation sym ∇X = −uK, (7.17) and Hess u = L(u, X, ∇X) + c 2 ∫ F∗ ν♭ F ⊗ ν♭ F dAF dπ(F). (7.18) The equations are distributional, and surface measures in the second equation are expressed relative to ambient volume. The operator L has smooth linear coefficients. It is specifically the lower-order operator from the metric adjoint in (7.11), with the flux form fixed and the unit-ball rays transported as specified above. In particular, it is not an arbitrary operator with smooth coefficients. Locally u is Lipschitz and X is C1,1. The complementarity relations (7.13) hold pointwise.
